newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW - Little enthusiasm seen at end of year.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Little enthusiasm seen at end of year.

text.p: As the IPO market winds down for 1996, a continuing short supply of quality issues and an uncertain market environment promise a lackluster reception for the 28 or so IPOs making their debuts this week.
"It's a sloppy environment that should become more treacherous as we go into the last weeks of pricing," said David Menlow, president of Springfield, New Jersey-based IPO Financial Network Corp.
"I'm not sure this market is going to reward a lot of IPOs", said Matt Considine, analyst at Phoenix Duff & Phelps.

Some issues this week do show promise, but analysts don't see anything very exciting. Vincent Slavin of Cantor Fitzgerald said he expects some premiums, "but they're not going to be blockbuster premiums."
A few technology deals look good to analysts, among them Coral Systems Inc, Procom Technology Inc and Larscom Inc. All three are Montgomery Securities' deals.

Analysts see a possible two-point jump for Coral Systems at the open. The Longmont, Colorado-based company provides client-server software products for the wireless telecommunications industry. The software allows carriers to reduce fraud and customer turnover.

"The driving force is that there is tremendous competition between wireless providers" as they try and reduce costs, said William Smith, analyst at Greenwich, Conn.-based Renaissance Capital Corp. Fraud detection and minimizing customer turnover is part of these efforts, he said.
Coral Systems is offering 2.7 million shares in a range of $10-$12 a share.
Larscom could also fetch an opening premium, analysts say.
"It's a well-established company with a strong product line," said Kathleen Smith, analyst at Renaissance Capital. "And it's adapting its products to some very hot areas."
The company, which makes high speed global internetworking solutions for network service providers and corporate users, is offering seven million class A shares at a price range of $12 to $14.

John Fitzgibbon of the IPO Aftermarket said Procom Technology could see a one-point opening premium. The company, based in Irvine, Calif., makes data storage and information access solutions that are compatible with major hardware platforms, operating systems and network protocols.
Procom is offering 3.025 million shares which are expected to price between $9 and $11 a share.
Another deal that analysts said could pick up a small premium is Swisher International Group Inc's IPO of six million Class A shares.
The cigar manufacturer's offering is expected to be priced in a range of $17 to $20. Merrill Lynch is the lead underwriter.

BA Merchant Services Inc, a unit of BankAmerica Corp, is also making its debut next week with a 14 million Class A share global offering lead managed by Goldman Sachs. Of those, 11.2 million shares are being offered in the U.S. at $14 to $16 a share.
Fitzgibbon said the stock could trade $1 to $1.50 higher on its first day.
Other deals that analysts said could generate some interest are Amscan Holdings Inc, Mastech Corp, Aftermarket Technnology Corp, Titan Exploration Inc, Delia's Inc, and NetSource Communications Inc.

Analysts said that after this past bonanza year for IPOs, the market for new issues is taking a breather and will start reviving in January. "The market's kind of exhausted right now", said Smith of Renaissance.
The IPO Insider predicts that new money from bonus' and 401(k)s will be directed into IPOs in the first quarter, particularly in view of expensive blue chip levels.
